findings.title: Shutting down shared FixedQueuePool on strategy close breaks consumer after partition rebalance
findings.body: `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__` creates a single `self.queue_pool = FixedQueuePool(...)` instance (line 133) and reuses it across `create_with_partitions` calls (line 255). In Arroyo, whenever a Kafka consumer group rebalance occurs, `StreamProcessor` revokes partitions by calling `strategy.close()` and `strategy.join()` on the current strategy, and then calls `factory.create_with_partitions(...)` for the new assignment. Because `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()` (line 338 of `queue_consumer.py`), all worker threads in `self.queue_pool` exit and all `queue.Queue` instances are permanently shut down. After the rebalance, the new `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` receives the already-shut-down `queue_pool`; every subsequent `submit()` call hits `work_queue.put()`, which raises `queue.ShutDown`. Because `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()` catches `Exception` and marks the offset completed (lines 317-325 of `queue_consumer.py`), the consumer will silently drop all messages after any rebalance while still committing their offsets to Kafka.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown abandons queued items and stops commit thread before workers drain
findings.body:
There are two issues in the shutdown sequence across `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` (lines 335-339) and `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` (lines 231-244):
1. `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` sets `worker.shutdown = True` on all workers before calling `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`. While `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` is intended to let workers drain remaining queued items until `q.get()` raises `queue.ShutDown`, `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` checks `while not self.shutdown:` on each iteration (line 129). As a result, each worker exits immediately after finishing at most one in-flight item, dropping all other items still queued.
2. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` stops and joins `self.commit_thread` *before* calling `self.queue_pool.shutdown()` and does not perform a final commit afterward. Offsets completed since the last 1-second commit tick or during queue draining are never committed.

findings.title: OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets skips over uncommitted offset gaps after a commit
findings.body: In `OffsetTracker.mark_committed()`, all offsets `<= offset` are removed from `self.all_offsets[partition]` (line 105). In `get_committable_offsets()`, the scan starts at `start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)` where `min_offset = min(all_offsets)` (lines 83-86). If offset 100 is committed and pruned from `all_offsets`, and offsets 102 and 103 are completed while offset 101 has not yet been added, `min_offset` is `102`, so `start = max(101, 102) = 102`. The loop then starts at 102, completely skips the missing offset 101, and reports 103 as committable. Once `partition in self.last_committed`, the contiguous check must start at `last_committed + 1`, not `max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)`.

findings.title: Background commit_thread invokes Arroyo's non-thread-safe commit callback concurrently
findings.body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` spawns a background `commit_thread` that periodically calls `self.commit_function(committable)`, which invokes the Arroyo `commit` callback passed to `create_with_partitions`. In Arroyo, `StreamProcessor`'s commit callback (`KafkaConsumer.stage_positions` and `KafkaConsumer.commit_offsets`) is not thread-safe and mutates internal offset dictionaries and consumer state without locks on the assumption that it is only called from the main `StreamProcessor` thread (e.g., inside `submit()` or `poll()`). Calling `commit` from a background thread races with `StreamProcessor._run_once()` polling and committing on the main thread. Performing the periodic commit check inside `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.poll()` (and once at shutdown after workers drain) keeps all consumer operations on the main thread.

findings.title: Queues in FixedQueuePool are unbounded, providing no backpressure to StreamProcessor
findings.body: Although `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy`'s docstring states that it provides "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", `FixedQueuePool` initializes each `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize` (unbounded). In Arroyo, `StreamProcessor` polls Kafka and calls `strategy.submit(message)` as fast as messages arrive until `submit` raises `MessageRejected`. Because `submit()` only decodes the payload in memory and pushes a `WorkItem` (including the full raw `Message`) onto an unbounded queue without ever raising `MessageRejected`, any slowdown in downstream worker processing will cause the consumer to buffer an unbounded number of messages and offsets in memory.

findings.title: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling asserts the opposite of actual behavior due to commit timing
findings.body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` states that "errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages", and `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` unconditionally marks offsets completed in its `finally` block (line 149 of `queue_consumer.py`) even when `result_processor` raises an exception. However, the test only waits `0.2s` after both items are processed (line 1917), while `_commit_loop` waits `1.0s` before committing (`self.shutdown_event.wait(1.0)`). Because the 1-second commit interval has not elapsed yet, `committed_offsets` is still empty and line 1922 asserts `assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`—the opposite of what happens once the commit loop runs (and if the test takes >= 1.0s on CI, the commit will fire and fail this assertion). Also note that calling `factory.shutdown()` without `consumer.close()` in these tests leaves `consumer.commit_thread` running in the background.
